prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Mission/scope: hospital automated medication dispensing and initial medication-return handling, covering order intake, pharmacy preparation/verification, and ward access. Workflow must support timely fulfillment while preserving pharmacist oversight, medication traceability, and clinical control.
Aliases: Cinderwake = Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper = Pharmacy Verification Station; Tallowmere = Medication Return Kiosk; Larkspur = Registered Nurse.
Elements, actors, and flows: Medication Order Gateway provides controlled medication-order entry and communicates order status to authorized hospital systems. Clinical Pharmacist reviews clinical appropriateness, resolves medication questions requiring professional judgment, and produces Dose Exception Review Slip when an order requires documented exception review. Pharmacy Technician performs routine preparation within approved procedures and escalates discrepancies to Clinical Pharmacist. Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot produces Priority Refill Tote Tag for eligible refill work, prepares eligible medication against the active order, and records handling actions. Pharmacy Verification Station supports final verification before medication release for delivery or ward access. Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler maintains monitored storage conditions for temperature-controlled medication. East Tube Dispatch Console and West Tube Dispatch Console provide controlled routing interfaces for authorized pharmacy deliveries. Pneumatic Tube Network carries compatible deliveries between designated hospital locations under established routing procedures. Charge Nurse coordinates ward readiness, communicates operational constraints, and supports escalation during dispensing-service disruption. Medication Return Kiosk records medication returns, captures return details, and produces Return Bin Audit Label for each recorded return transaction. Hospital Courier supports authorized movement of medication and returns when automated routes are unavailable or unsuitable. Biomedical Engineer maintains supported equipment; IT Operations Specialist monitors connectivity and service availability.
Requirements: ward medication access remains subject to local authorization, patient-care requirements, and applicable cabinet controls. Returned medication must remain segregated from usable stock until disposition is assessed under hospital procedure. No explicit operating modes defined.

New part:
S025: The Medication Safety Officer oversees safety concerns, reviews relevant trends, and supports updates to medication handling procedures.
S026: The Medication Order Gateway is called Morrowglass in this concept.
S027: The Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler is called Bluejay in this concept.
S028: The Pharmacy Technician is called Copperfield in this concept.
S029: The Medication Order Gateway accepts medication orders from authorized clinical systems and records their arrival times.
S030: It checks required order fields, patient identifiers, medication codes, quantities, and destination details before routing an order for pharmacy review.
S031: The gateway flags missing data, duplicate submissions, and changes that conflict with the active order record.
S032: The Medication Order Gateway produces the Order Reconciliation Snapshot for documenting detected order discrepancies.
S033: The Pharmacy Verification Station displays queued orders and their validation results for review.
S034: The Clinical Pharmacist evaluates clinical appropriateness, dose limits, allergies, and relevant interactions before approving an order.
S035: The Pharmacy Technician investigates administrative discrepancies and requests clarification through approved clinical channels.
S036: Unresolved discrepancies keep an order from advancing to preparation.
S037: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot prepares only orders that have passed the required review and authorization checks.
S038: The Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler maintains refrigerated medications within the facility's approved temperature range.
S039: Continuous sensors record temperature readings and report excursions or loss of monitoring connectivity.
S040: The Pharmacy Technician checks the cooler's status and confirms that refrigerated stock remains within handling limits before use.
S041: The Pharmacy Technician produces the Cold Chain Handoff Card to document custody and handling conditions.
S042: When an excursion occurs, affected stock is segregated pending assessment and disposition by authorized pharmacy staff.
S043: Temperature records are retained with timestamps so reviewers can establish the duration and extent of an excursion.
S044: The Clinical Pharmacist determines whether affected medication remains suitable for dispensing under approved procedures.
S045: The Pharmacy Technician checks packaging, product identity, lot details, and expiry information during routine stock handling.
S046: The Medication Safety Officer reviews patterns of discrepancies and handling events for potential safety concerns.
S047: The Medication Safety Officer produces the Diversion Review Packet when a diversion concern requires documented review.
S048: The Pharmacy Verification Station preserves review decisions and order status changes in an auditable record.
S049: Orders remain unavailable for dispensing until required checks are complete and their status is authorized.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
